title: Publish Codex provider runtime surface
description: Objective: make the landed Codex runtime adapter operationally reachable from the @moe/runner package root so production consumers and the portability shadow gate can invoke the same immutable observation, probe, stream, render, cancellation, and reconciliation surface rather than deep-importing or reimplementing it. Deliverable: a curated Codex surface module, NodeNext bridge, root exports, and root/runtime surface tests. NOT in scope: daemon dispatch, provider launch, new Codex behavior, or telemetry. Measured at HEAD 30458af: packages/runner/src/providers/codex/** exists from task-a0fa6da4024647d69c25d273b217eaeb, but @moe/runner publishes only ProbeCodexRuntimeInput/report type closure through recovery inventory; operational Codex builders/classifiers are absent from the bare root. Consumers: task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93 and the future provider dispatch service. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/surface/codex-surface.ts/.js, packages/runner/src/index.ts, packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts, packages/runner/src/runtime-entrypoint.test.ts.
definitionOfDone: The bare @moe/runner root exposes a deliberately curated operational Codex surface covering runtime observation/probe, capability vocabulary, stream recording, render output, cancellation, and reconciliation without exporting test fixtures or internal authority helpers.
All published values and their directly named type closure resolve through NodeNext .js bridges; a compiled bare-specifier type probe and a plain-Node runtime probe both exit 0.
Hand-written surface assertions pin the exact non-empty new runtime names and preserve every existing root export; deleting or aliasing one production export makes the focused test red.
No Codex behavior, provider lifecycle, or authority semantics change; task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93 is recorded as the acceptance consumer.
taskRails: Do not blanket-export providers/codex/**; expose only reviewed public capability values/types.
Do not add a daemon consumer or claim launch authority in this surface task.
Every runtime module gets an exact LF .js bridge and plain-Node loadability coverage.

implementationPlan.description: Derive the AUTHORITATIVE collision set before writing a line of surface code. My planning extractors found 25 codex export names already present at the @moe/runner root, but BOTH extractors miss single-line `export type { X } from "..."` forms (ProbeCodexRuntimeInput is a known miss), so treat my list as a floor, not a total. Re-derive it properly, e.g.: extract every name the four existing surface modules and index.ts publish (handle both the multi-line `  Name,` / `  type Name,` form AND the single-line `export type { Name } from` form), intersect with the exports of packages/runner/src/providers/codex/*.ts, and record the result. Then classify every hit into exactly one of two families, because they need OPPOSITE treatment: FAMILY A = provider-neutral names where codex has its own DUPLICATE implementation (codex-observation.ts and claude-observation.ts share 17 export names and codex-observation imports only ../../canonical.js, so they are genuinely separate code) - these MUST be aliased. FAMILY B = Codex-prefixed types recovery-inventory-surface.ts ALREADY publishes from the same codex modules (lines 86 and 97) - these must NOT be re-exported at all, because recovery-inventory-surface.ts is not an owned path and two owners for one name is a hygiene defect, not a fix. Record both lists in the surface module's doc comment.

Codex total 101 names across 8 modules — matches the planning note.

implementationPlan.note:
TYPE CLOSURE PROVEN. All 42 published Codex types imported from the bare `@moe/runner` specifier and used to annotate REAL values returned by the seam — never a bare literal, which would typecheck against a locally re-declared shape whether or not the type ever published. WHY THE ANNOTATIONS ARE LOAD-BEARING HERE. tsconfig.base.json sets `noUnusedLocals: true` and `verbatimModuleSyntax: true`. So an unpublished name fails as TS2305 at the import, and a name imported but never driven fails as TS6192/TS6133. Both directions are enforced by the compiler, and typecheck reports ZERO errors in index-surface.test.ts — that is the assertion step 5 asked for. The same rule is visible working on a foreign file right now (TS6133 on an unused local in claude-launch-verify.ts), so it is demonstrably live, not assumed.

- buildCodexRuntimeObservation: OK arm (observation annotated, version/providerId/truthClass checked) and REFUSED arm via a closure entry whose sha256 is a well-typed string but not 64-hex -> CODEX_OBSERVATION_CLOSURE_INVALID.

- probeCodexRuntime: OK arm, and every record in the returned profile asserted to be a member of all three published vocabularies.
- reconcileCodexRun composes ON the stream record from the previous call, so the test proves the two seams actually chain rather than merely coexisting.

THREE WRONG ASSUMPTIONS OF MINE, ALL CAUGHT BY THE TESTS AND CORRECTED AGAINST PRODUCTION — recording them because each was a guess that a laxer assertion would have hidden:
1. I asserted `codexObservationDigestInput` returns a string. It returns `Record<string, unknown>` — the digest INPUT, not the digest. Now asserts it reproduces providerId/observationVersion/truthClass AND that `observationDigest` is absent from it, which is the property that actually matters.
2. I asserted CODEX_PROOF_METHODS has 5 members. It has 12. Counts now read [12, 2, 12, 2] against the real vocabularies.
3. The skill-file fixture used a placeholder sha256; the renderer re-hashes decoded content and refused with "skill file SKILL.md digest differs". Now carries the true sha256 of the decoded bytes.

THE MOST IMPORTANT CORRECTION — WHICH LAYER REFUSED. I had asserted `renderCodexAdvisorySkills` refuses an unsupported `rendererInputVersion`. It does not: that gate lives in `renderCodexContext.validateSnapshot` alone, and the skills renderer renders a bad-version snapshot happily. The two published entry points do NOT share a gate. Rather than delete the assertion I pinned both directions, which is strictly stronger and is what epic rail 6 asks for when more than one layer can refuse: renderCodexAdvisorySkills(badVersion) still returns Uint8Array, renderCodexContext(badVersion) refuses CODEX_RENDER_SKILL_SNAPSHOT_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED, and the skills renderer's OWN gate is driven separately with a non-recomputing file digest -> CODEX_RENDER_SKILL_SNAPSHOT_INVALID. Asserting only "it refused" would have let either gate answer for the other and stayed green forever.

THREE WAYS THIS TEST IS KEPT FROM GOING VACUOUS, each a failure mode I have hit or recorded before:
1. COMMENTS ARE STRIPPED FIRST. codex-surface.ts's doc comment lists all ten Family B names precisely to explain why it does NOT republish them. A raw text match would read that prose as a second owner and fail for a false reason — the boundary-scan-matches-comments defect.
2. THE STRIPPER HAS A POSITIVE CONTROL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a stripper that removes too much finds zero owners and passes silently. Asserted: the raw codex-surface source CONTAINS "CodexCancelObservation" while the stripped source does NOT, and the stripped source still CONTAINS "probeCodexRuntime". Under-stripping and over-stripping both go red.
3. THE CASE LIST IS GUARDED. `expect(SURFACE_SOURCES.size).toBe(5)` plus an exact filename set equality. An empty or narrowed enumeration would satisfy every assertion below it while measuring nothing.
